subject: Clarifying VAT treatment for cross-border consignment and invoice ownership
messages:
From: Sara Jansen <sara.jansen@olivetech.com>

Cc: Armin Schultz <armin.schultz@eurolog.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T07:45:00Z
Subject: VAT treatment for consignment stock / invoice ownership

Hi Karthik,

Quick question from OliveTech's logistics and finance team. We're moving a batch of demo units to the EU warehouse you manage under the consignment agreement we discussed. Two things we need to confirm before we finalize shipping and invoicing:

1) VAT point: under EU rules, do we only consider a supply (and VAT liability) when the customer takes ownership from consignment, or is there any reporting required when goods are simply moved into consignment stock?

2) Invoice ownership: OliveTech would typically issue the invoice when legal title transfers, but our buyer (EuroLogistics) is asking if Redwood can instead issue a pro forma invoice at goods transfer time and OliveTech will self-bill afterwards. We want to avoid duplicate VAT tagging and ensure the reverse-charge / margin-scheme implications are handled correctly.

Attached are the draft consignment SLA and our preferred invoice template for context. Can you confirm what Redwood needs on the invoice and whether we should expect any withholding or other collection quirks for intra-EU moves under this flow?

Thanks — short turnaround would be appreciated, this shipment is penciled for July 26.

Best,
Sara Jansen
Head of Finance Operations
OliveTech

Sara — thanks for the clear note. Looping in Marissa (Tax & Billing) and Ben (Collections) to get precise guidance and the operational steps. Quick, high-level: my understanding is that consignment typically isn't a taxable supply until title passes — but there are nuances by member state and whether the movement is treated as an intra-community transfer or a domestic receipt.

Marissa/Ben — can you confirm: (A) whether Redwood should accept a self-bill from OliveTech post-transfer, (B) whether we need to issue any movement-related records that trigger VAT registration/reporting, and (C) recommended invoice fields to avoid double-tax tagging in our billing pipeline? Sara noted the buyer prefers Redwood to issue a pro forma at transfer.

I'll hold shipment until we have the final go-ahead for invoicing and any PO updates.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Manager, EMEA
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: VAT treatment for cross-border consignment and invoice ownership

Karthik / Sara — explained below is our recommended approach based on EU VAT practice and the example member-states OliveTech mentioned on the SLA. Attaching the marked-up SLA with a short checklist.

Summary guidance (short):
- Consignment stock: generally not a taxable supply at the time of movement into consignment. The taxable event is the transfer of title / sale out of consignment to the final buyer. That means VAT is accounted for at point of transfer, normally by the supplier (OliveTech) unless parties agree to self-billing.
- Self-billing option: allowed, but requires a prior written agreement between supplier and buyer. If Redwood is asked to issue the invoice on OliveTech's behalf (self-billing), we need: the signed self-billing agreement, confirmation of the VAT treatment to apply (e.g., standard-rated supply vs margin-scheme), and OliveTech's VAT ID. Without that we should not issue supplier invoices that substitute OliveTech's VAT point.
- Reverse-charge: typically not applicable for intra-EU supplies of goods when ownership passes in another member state (normal intra-community supply rules apply). Reverse-charge is more common for services. That said, if the sale is treated as domestic in buyer's country due to where supply takes place, buyer-side adjustments may be needed.
- Invoice fields to prevent double-tax tagging in Redwood billing: include supplier VAT ID, buyer VAT ID, clear statement 'Supply of goods — consignment transfer of ownership', shipment date, transfer-of-ownership date (if known), and a reference to the signed self-billing agreement ID. If OliveTech prefers Redwood to issue a pro forma at transfer, mark it explicitly 'Pro forma — no tax liability; final invoice to follow' unless a self-billing agreement is in place.

Operational next steps (to be completed before July 26 shipment):
1) OliveTech: send signed self-billing agreement (or confirm you do not want Redwood to self-bill).
2) OliveTech: provide VAT IDs for the supplying and buying entities.
3) Redwood collections: Ben to flag whether we need a billing hold or alternate remittance path while we confirm VAT IDs.
4) Redwood tax: we will run a quick jurisdiction check on where the legal supply occurs; if supply is considered intra-community, we'll record it as such and no ECC reversal is needed.

Ben — can you confirm whether a temporary collections hold is required until we have VAT IDs and the self-billing agreement? I've attached the SLA with inline notes.

Marissa Cole
Director, Tax & Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
